title: TTL staleness triggered routing oscillation - postmortem
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2026-03-10 at ~03:12 UTC, Redwood experienced a multi-region routing oscillation that caused a sustained surge of fallback requests to lower-tier model variants for ~18 minutes. Symptoms included increased 95th/99th latency for hosted customers routed through eu-west and us-central, a sharp rise in fallback rate (from baseline ~0.3% to 12%), and temporary quota/soft-limit pressure on fallback nodes. Impact: several production customers observed degraded response times and increased costs due to repeated fallback hits and repeated re-tries. Incident magnitude was P0 due to violation of latency SLOs and customer-facing errors.

Timeline (condensed):
- 03:06 UTC: control-plane deploy (platform/config rollout job) completed a scheduled micro-config change to capacity hint TTL (intended from 10s -> 30s) as part of an autoscaling tuning campaign (release runtime-1.22).
- 03:11 UTC: heartbeat aggregator service (routing-heartbeat) began processing heartbeats after a brief GC pause on a coordinator node. A bug in the aggregator codepath caused TTL refreshes to be ignored for heartbeats that matched a deprecated checksum (introduced in routing-heartbeat v2.4.1). The service accepted older capacity_hint entries without updating their TTLs.
- 03:12 UTC: Region-level routing weight recalculation job consumed stale capacity_hint entries from aggregator (the entries showed several eu-west nodes as low-capacity due to an earlier transient drain), because TTLs had expired logically but not refreshed in the aggregator cache. The weight calculator deprioritized eu-west and us-central by 60-80%.
- 03:12-03:20 UTC: Traffic shifted off eu-west/us-central into fallback tiers and alternative regions. Fallback variant pool in us-east reached soft safety caps; continuous reroutes to remaining fallback nodes increased their latency and triggered additional load shedding, amplifying the fallback cascade.
- 03:20 UTC: Alerting fired for unusual fallback-rate and weight-change velocity. SRE on-call manually pinned routing weights to prior snapshot and rolled back the TTL change.
- 03:28 UTC: Hotfix PR merged to routing-heartbeat to fix TTL refresh logic (https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/9876). Hotfix deployed to control plane and aggregator fleet.
- 03:34 UTC: Normalized routing weights; fallback rate returned to baseline by ~03:40 UTC.

Root cause analysis (short):
- Primary root cause: A logic regression in routing-heartbeat (v2.4.1) prevented TTL refresh for capacity_hint entries that matched a deprecated checksum path. As a result, the aggregator exposed stale capacity hints to downstream weight recalculation.
- Secondary contributing factors:
  - A concurrent config change increased TTL expectation (10s -> 30s) but the aggregator bug meant perceived TTLs were stale/incorrectly recorded.
  - Weight recalculation job lacked a validation gate to compare significant weight deltas against recent traffic telemetry (velocity guard). Large sudden weight changes were applied without circuit-breaker.
  - Fallback soft-cap signaling is conservative but depended on timely regional weight adjustments; cascade amplified because fallback pool soft limits were hit before automatic fallback throttles engaged.

Why this caused an oscillation: stale hints caused large, asymmetric deprioritization of specific regions. The traffic displacement overloaded fallback variants; as fallback variants slowed, routing began deprioritizing those nodes too, causing more displacement to the remaining pools in a positive feedback loop until manual intervention.

Mitigations performed during incident:
- Immediate: Rolled back TTL config change, pinned routing weights to last-known-good snapshot, and disabled weight-recalculator cron for 15 minutes to stop further oscillation.
- Hotfix: Patch to routing-heartbeat merged (PR #9876) and rolled out to aggregator fleet to restore correct TTL refresh behavior.
- Throttle: Temporarily increased fallback soft caps and enabled emergency per-region traffic caps to allow gradual rebalancing.

Long-term corrective actions (planned / owner / ETA):
- Add a weight-change velocity guard in the weight recalculation service that rejects or canaries >20% single-step weight shifts (owner: Marcus Chen, ETA: 2026-04-04).
- Improve aggregator TTL instrumentation (emit TTL freshness histograms and stale-hint alarms) (owner: Priya Nair, ETA: 2026-03-28).
- Harden unit/integration tests for the heartbeat TTL path to cover checksum-matching edge cases (owner: Eng Test, ETA: 2026-03-21).
- Implement cascading-fallback early throttle that caps fallback activation rate across tiers to avoid pool exhaustion (owner: Reliability Team, ETA: 2026-04-11).
- Post-deploy canary: add a short canary window for config changes that affect TTL/weighting (owner: Platform Releases, ETA: 2026-03-31).
- Incident retro doc and runbook updates: update routing runbook with commands to pin weights, rollback TTLs, and emergency fallback cap commands (owner: SRE Docs, ETA: 2026-03-18). Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/TTL+Stale+Routing+Postmortem

Monitoring and alerts added:
- fallback-rate > 1% absolute and > 3x baseline for 2 minutes -> PagerDuty critical (owner: Observability)
- weight-change velocity > 15% in 30s -> Alert and automatic canary freeze of recalculator
- aggregator TTL-staleness ratio > 5% -> Alert (new metric emitted by routing-heartbeat)

Follow-ups and tracking tickets:
- ENG-43210: implement velocity guard in weight recalculator
- ENG-43211: TTL instrumentation and alerts for routing-heartbeat
- ENG-43212: cascading-fallback throttle design
- ENG-43213: test coverage for heartbeat checksum/TTL codepath

Post-incident notes and learnings:
- Small changes that touch TTLs or heartbeat semantics can have outsized system effects because TTLs function as soft signals that inform routing decisions. We must treat TTL and heartbeat semantics as high-sensitivity config with canary and review gates.
- The control-plane must not expose single-source-of-truth blind spots: aggregator caches should aggressively annotate freshness and be conservative when freshness is unknown.
- Rapid manual mitigation by SRE (pinning weights) prevented a longer outage; however we need automated guardrails to avoid manual-only recovery.
